projects.name: FieldOps Dispatch App
projects.description: Offline-capable field service dispatch application for regional utility contractors.
projects.objective: Coordinate crews, work orders, parts, route changes, and safety checkpoints with reliable sync under weak connectivity.

nodes.title: Offline-first architecture
nodes.subtitle: Local command queue plus conflict-aware sync
nodes.notes: The mobile client keeps a local event log for work order transitions, photo captures, inventory reservations, and safety attestations. Sync is append-only from the client and resolved server-side with explicit conflict states instead of silent last-write-wins behavior.

nodes.title: Use server-authoritative conflict records
nodes.subtitle: No automatic overwrite when crew and dispatcher edit the same task
nodes.notes: Conflicts become first-class records with involved fields, actor ids, timestamps, and recommended resolution. Dispatch supervisors get a queue with field-safe summaries. The decision reduces data loss risk but adds workflow complexity.

nodes.title: Crew mobile workflow
nodes.subtitle: Route, checklist, evidence, and parts capture
nodes.notes: The app must support route manifests, job start/stop, checklist completion, photo evidence, signature capture, part consumption, and a daily closeout packet. All actions must work when the device is offline for a full shift.

nodes.title: Dispatcher console
nodes.subtitle: Exception-driven scheduling board
nodes.notes: Dispatchers need a dense board focused on late crews, route exceptions, blocked parts, and customer access risks. The console should not mimic the mobile flow; it should prioritize scanning and rapid reassignment.

nodes.title: ERP and GIS integrations
nodes.subtitle: Work orders, materials, and map layers
nodes.notes: ERP is source of truth for work orders and inventory; GIS is source of truth for assets and outage polygons. Integration events should carry correlation ids and external version fields to support audit and replay.

nodes.title: Safety and liability risk
nodes.subtitle: Auditability is more important than UI convenience
nodes.notes: Safety checklist bypasses, missing photos, and clock skew can create liability exposure. The system must log bypass reason, actor, device time, server receive time, and downstream reviewer decision.

nodes.title: Connectivity and conflict test matrix
nodes.subtitle: Weak network, duplicate upload, and concurrent edit cases
nodes.notes: Test cases include airplane-mode shift, duplicate media upload after retry, supervisor resolves crew-dispatcher conflict, inventory reservation revoked by ERP, and daylight-saving boundary on scheduled work.

nodes.title: Pilot readiness gate
nodes.subtitle: Two crews, one dispatcher, staged ERP sync
nodes.notes: Pilot starts only after sync replay is deterministic, conflict records are visible in the dispatcher console, and safety evidence can be exported as a signed packet.

projects.name: LedgerLens Compliance SaaS
projects.description: B2B SaaS for finance teams that need continuous revenue recognition and audit evidence checks.
projects.objective: Detect revenue recognition policy drift, produce evidence packs, and reduce audit preparation time for mid-market SaaS companies.

nodes.title: Target segment
nodes.subtitle: Controller-led SaaS finance teams
nodes.notes: Initial buyers are companies with 50 to 500 employees, contract changes, usage-based pricing, and an annual audit cycle. The wedge is policy drift detection rather than replacing the general ledger.

nodes.title: Position as audit evidence automation
nodes.subtitle: Avoid claiming autonomous accounting judgement
nodes.notes: The safer value proposition is evidence completeness, policy exception surfacing, and reviewer workflow. The system should recommend attention, not independently recognize revenue.

nodes.title: Core product loops
nodes.subtitle: Ingest, test, explain, review, export
nodes.notes: The product imports contract metadata, invoices, payment events, product usage, and policy definitions. It runs rules, explains exceptions, routes review tasks, and exports auditor-ready evidence bundles.

nodes.title: Pricing model
nodes.subtitle: Platform fee plus entity and transaction tiers
nodes.notes: Pricing should align with audit complexity: base platform fee, legal-entity tier, and high-volume event surcharge. Avoid per-seat-only pricing because evidence workflows expand to auditors temporarily.

nodes.title: Data boundary
nodes.subtitle: Financial data minimization and tenant isolation
nodes.notes: Tenant isolation is mandatory. Store normalized event hashes and policy snapshots; limit raw document retention. Logs must not include contract values, customer names, or bank references.

nodes.title: Adoption risks
nodes.subtitle: Trust, liability, and integration fatigue
nodes.notes: Finance teams will reject opaque automation. The roadmap must budget for explainability, audit trails, and connector maintenance. Integration fatigue is a bigger risk than rule-engine performance.

nodes.title: Design partner package
nodes.subtitle: Narrow launch with three controllers and one audit advisor
nodes.notes: Offer fixed-fee onboarding, manual connector support, quarterly evidence-pack review, and a written limitation statement that the customer remains accounting decision owner.

nodes.title: Proof metric
nodes.subtitle: Audit prep hours and exception false-positive rate
nodes.notes: The pilot succeeds when evidence pack preparation drops by 40 percent and false positives stay below the controller's review tolerance. Track escaped exceptions discovered by auditors.

projects.name: Docker Delivery Platform Analysis
projects.description: Architecture analysis for standardizing Docker-based development and deployment across several internal products.
projects.objective: Reduce environment drift, speed onboarding, and define the boundary between local containers, CI images, and production runtime images.

nodes.title: Container baseline
nodes.subtitle: One contract for dev, CI, and release images
nodes.notes: Define base image ownership, image labels, health checks, non-root runtime users, SBOM generation, and version pinning. Development containers may add tooling but must not hide production dependencies.

nodes.title: Local compose topology
nodes.subtitle: App, database, queue, observability, and seeded fixtures
nodes.notes: Compose files should provide repeatable databases, message brokers, fake external services, and tracing collectors. The topology must avoid port collisions and support named profiles for heavy dependencies.

nodes.title: CI image pipeline
nodes.subtitle: Build once, scan, test, and promote
nodes.notes: The CI path should build immutable images once, run unit and integration tests against the same image digest, scan vulnerabilities, sign images, and promote by digest rather than rebuilding per environment.

nodes.title: No secrets in image layers
nodes.subtitle: Runtime injection only
nodes.notes: Build-time secrets are allowed only through ephemeral build mounts. Images must be scanned for secret patterns before promotion. Local `.env` files remain ignored and documented with sample placeholders.

nodes.title: Persistent state risk
nodes.subtitle: Volumes can mask migration and seed drift
nodes.notes: Developers often keep volumes too long, which hides schema migration problems. The platform needs explicit reset commands, migration checks, and fixture version stamps.

nodes.title: Developer experience
nodes.subtitle: Fast start without pretending containers are free
nodes.notes: The target is a reliable first run under fifteen minutes and a common diagnosis path for port, volume, image, and network problems. Heavy services should be opt-in profiles.

nodes.title: Container observability
nodes.subtitle: Logs, metrics, traces, and health semantics
nodes.notes: Standardize stdout log fields, readiness and liveness endpoints, OpenTelemetry resource attributes, and per-service dashboards. Local observability should reveal startup failures without attaching debuggers.

nodes.title: First service migration
nodes.subtitle: One product as reference implementation
nodes.notes: Select a service with a database, background worker, and external API dependency. The migration is not done until a new developer can run it from a clean machine and CI promotes signed images.

projects.name: Regional Economy And Household Budget Study
projects.description: Non-programming analysis of household budget pressure in a mid-sized region affected by rent growth, food prices, and wage lag.
projects.objective: Map causal drivers, identify practical household and local-policy interventions, and separate short-term stress from structural vulnerability.

nodes.title: Income pattern
nodes.subtitle: Wage growth is uneven across households
nodes.notes: Median wages rose, but service-sector households face unstable hours and delayed wage gains. Dual-income households are resilient until child-care or transport disruptions reduce hours.

nodes.title: Housing cost pressure
nodes.subtitle: Rent renewal shock is the largest recurring stressor
nodes.notes: Rent increases concentrate budget stress because they are recurring and hard to substitute. Households respond by moving farther from jobs, which shifts pressure into transport and time costs.

nodes.title: Food and household staples
nodes.subtitle: Small price changes create weekly cash-flow volatility
nodes.notes: Food inflation affects low-income households through timing as much as total cost. Weekly cash shortages increase reliance on high-fee credit and reduce preventive health spending.

nodes.title: Transport tradeoff
nodes.subtitle: Long commutes convert cheaper rent into hidden cost
nodes.notes: Households moving outward often lose savings to fuel, maintenance, insurance, and missed shifts. Transit improvements matter when schedules align with shift work, not only office commutes.

nodes.title: Prioritize cash-flow stabilization
nodes.subtitle: Small predictable supports beat complex programs
nodes.notes: The study recommends emergency rent mediation, utility payment smoothing, employer shift predictability, and grocery price transparency before broader subsidy proposals.

nodes.title: Interpretation risks
nodes.subtitle: Avoid single-cause explanations
nodes.notes: The analysis should avoid blaming one category such as rent or groceries. Household stress emerges from correlated shocks, weak buffers, and timing mismatch between income and bills.

nodes.title: Measurement plan
nodes.subtitle: Track volatility, not only averages
nodes.notes: Use monthly rent burden, weekly food basket variance, missed-shift count, credit-fee incidence, and emergency assistance wait time as leading indicators.

nodes.title: Policy brief delivery
nodes.subtitle: Readable memo for local council and community groups
nodes.notes: The final brief should separate evidence, assumptions, and proposed experiments. It must explain why cash-flow timing matters and identify which interventions can be piloted in ninety days.

projects.name: Clinic Operations Redesign
projects.description: Non-software process redesign for a small outpatient clinic experiencing long wait times and inconsistent follow-up.
projects.objective: Reduce patient wait time, improve follow-up reliability, and clarify staff responsibilities without adding headcount.

nodes.title: Patient intake
nodes.subtitle: Pre-visit preparation and front-desk triage
nodes.notes: The current intake process mixes insurance updates, symptom capture, and document collection at arrival. Move predictable work to pre-visit outreach and reserve front-desk time for exceptions.

nodes.title: Rooming workflow
nodes.subtitle: Standardize vitals, medication review, and escalation
nodes.notes: Medical assistants need a stable checklist and clear escalation path for missing medication lists, red-flag symptoms, and language support. Variation in rooming creates physician delays.

nodes.title: Follow-up reliability
nodes.subtitle: Close the loop on labs, referrals, and calls
nodes.notes: Follow-up tasks should be visible in one queue with owner, due date, patient contact status, and blocker. The queue must not rely on memory or informal notes.

nodes.title: Assign queue owner by task type
nodes.subtitle: Avoid shared invisible ownership
nodes.notes: Lab results, referral scheduling, prescription questions, and patient portal messages need explicit role ownership. Shared responsibility without triage rules is the current failure mode.

nodes.title: Constraints
nodes.subtitle: No additional headcount and limited system changes
nodes.notes: The redesign must work with current staff and the existing EHR. It can add checklists, huddles, queue conventions, and manual reports, but not a large software replacement.

nodes.title: Two-week pilot
nodes.subtitle: One provider team with daily huddle review
nodes.notes: Pilot scope includes pre-visit outreach, standardized rooming checklist, and follow-up queue review. Capture wait time, staff overtime, unresolved follow-ups, and patient call-backs.

nodes.title: Operational metrics
nodes.subtitle: Median wait, ninety-fifth percentile wait, and follow-up age
nodes.notes: Track patient wait from arrival to clinician, room turnover, percentage of visits with completed pre-work, follow-up queue age, and number of reopened patient contacts.

nodes.title: Staff training plan
nodes.subtitle: Role-specific job aids and escalation examples
nodes.notes: Training should be practical: front desk exceptions, assistant rooming scripts, clinician handoff expectations, and manager queue review. Avoid generic process diagrams without desk-level examples.

projects.name: Community Learning Program
projects.description: Non-programming initiative for adult digital literacy, job readiness, and local mentorship.
projects.objective: Build a repeatable twelve-week program that helps adults gain practical digital skills and connect to local employment pathways.

nodes.title: Learner profile
nodes.subtitle: Adults with mixed device access and uneven confidence
nodes.notes: Participants may have smartphones but limited laptop access, inconsistent internet, and prior negative experiences with school. The program must build confidence through useful tasks, not abstract lectures.

nodes.title: Curriculum arc
nodes.subtitle: Devices, documents, communication, job tasks, and safety
nodes.notes: The twelve-week arc covers device basics, email, forms, document editing, spreadsheets for household budgets, job applications, video calls, and online safety. Each session ends with a concrete artifact.

nodes.title: Mentor network
nodes.subtitle: Local volunteers and employer partners
nodes.notes: Mentors support practice labs and provide context about workplace expectations. The program needs boundaries so mentors do not become unofficial case managers.

nodes.title: Access barriers
nodes.subtitle: Transport, child care, device availability, and language
nodes.notes: Attendance barriers may dominate curriculum quality. The design includes flexible lab hours, loaner devices, child-friendly waiting space, and bilingual support for high-demand sessions.

nodes.title: Partnerships
nodes.subtitle: Library, workforce board, employers, and community groups
nodes.notes: The library provides space and devices, the workforce board helps with job pathways, employers provide mock tasks, and community groups handle outreach. Each partner needs a clear commitment.

nodes.title: Outcome measurement
nodes.subtitle: Attendance, artifacts, confidence, and job-pathway progress
nodes.notes: Measure completed artifacts, participant confidence, continued lab use, applications submitted, interviews scheduled, and mentor follow-up. Avoid reducing success to job placement alone.

nodes.title: First cohort launch
nodes.subtitle: Fifteen learners, two mentors per lab night
nodes.notes: The first cohort is capped to preserve support quality. Launch requires lesson kits, mentor orientation, device inventory, attendance protocol, and escalation plan for social-service needs.

nodes.title: Sustainability plan
nodes.subtitle: Funding, volunteer retention, and partner accountability
nodes.notes: Funding should cover coordinator time, devices, connectivity, translation, and participant transportation support. Volunteer retention depends on clear schedules and visible learner progress.
